title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let \hat\pi_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,\infty}. It is free profinite on loops l_0, l_1, l_\infty with l_\infty l_1 l_0 = 1 (or a similar ordering). Two finite-order automorphisms act on it:
- \rho, of order 3, cyclically permuting the punctures (l_0 -> l_1 -> l_\infty);
- \sigma_\infty, of order 2, swapping 0 and 1 and fixing \infty.
Grothendieck studies the group Aut_loc(\hat C^+_{0,3}, \sigma_\infty)' of 'local' automorphisms u of the genus-0 Teichmueller tower at level (0,3). This is the precursor of what Drinfeld later (1990) called \widehat{GT}.

The parametrization (previous page). Such a u is given by a pair (\xi, \gamma), with \xi in \hat\pi_{0,3} and \gamma in \hat Z, subject to:
- (63) 2\gamma+1 is in \hat Z^*;
- (64) the 3-cycle relation \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi) = 1;
- (68) the 2-cycle relation \sigma_\infty(\xi) = l_1^\gamma \xi^{-1} l_0^\gamma;
- (d) further 'boundary' conditions coming from level (0,4), which give back (53).
In Drinfeld's notation this is the pair (\lambda, f) with \lambda = 2m+1. Here \gamma plays the role of m, the unit p = 2\gamma+1 plays the role of the cyclotomic character, and \xi is essentially f (up to normalization). Two pairs give the same u iff \gamma = \gamma' and \xi' = l_0^{-\alpha} \xi l_1^{\alpha} (69). This reflects the ambiguity of choosing the tangential base point / the conjugation by the inertia at 0.

This page, part 1. The 3-cocycle condition (64) is solved parametrically (70). Either \xi = \lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1}, a coboundary for the Z/3-action, or \xi = \lambda l_0^{-1}\rho(\lambda)^{-1}, a coboundary twisted by the order-3 torsion class. Indeed in the second case
\xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi) = \lambda (l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1} l_\infty^{-1}) \lambda^{-1} = 1.
Substituting into (68) gives the 'equations in \lambda' (71):
- \sigma_\infty(\lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1}) = l_1^\gamma (\rho(\lambda)\lambda^{-1}) l_0^\gamma, or
- \sigma_\infty(\lambda l_0^{-1}\rho(\lambda)^{-1}) = l_1^\gamma (\rho(\lambda) l_0 \lambda^{-1}) l_0^\gamma.
The residual ambiguity becomes (72): \lambda' = l_0^{-\alpha}\lambda, with \gamma unchanged.

This page, Remark 1. Up to the 'cyclotomic factor' l_0^\gamma, which is what distinguishes h_0 from \xi (cf. (65)), the data of u is equivalent to a simultaneous solution of two non-abelian 1-cocycle equations (73):
- \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi) = 1, for Z/3 acting via \rho;
- h_0\sigma_\infty(h_0) = 1, for Z/2 acting via \sigma_\infty.
Their parametric solutions (74) are:
- \xi = \lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1} or \xi = \lambda l_0^{-1}\rho(\lambda)^{-1}, according to \gamma mod 3, i.e. the cyclotomic unit p mod 3;
- h_0 = g_0^{-1}\sigma_\infty(g_0) (with some exponent/twist).
In modern terms, the two components of a GT-element are read as classes in the non-abelian cohomology sets H^1(Z/3, \hat\pi_{0,3}) and H^1(Z/2, \hat\pi_{0,3}). The case split corresponds to the two conjugacy classes of order-3 'sections', i.e. elliptic points of order 3: the trivial class and the class of the torsion element l_0-twist. The parameter p mod 3 decides which class occurs.

This page, margin. The expression (62) for \sigma_\infty exhibits \sigma_\infty as inner, presumably inside an orbifold or extended group containing \hat\pi_{0,3}.

What it serves. Solving and structuring the defining equations of the Teichmueller-tower automorphism group (proto-\widehat{GT}) and its Galois image. The next page proposes to view \lambda, g_0, h_0, ... as universal functions on this group and hence on \Gamma_Q.
errors: Case condition mod 3 as written looks inconsistent. Since p = 2\gamma+1 must be a unit, \gamma ≡ 1 (mod 3) would give p ≡ 0 (mod 3), which is excluded. The admissible cases are \gamma ≡ 0 (p ≡ 1) and \gamma ≡ 2 ≡ -1 (p ≡ -1). The written '\sigma≡1 (3)' (with the 1 apparently overwritten) should presumably read -1, or 2.

The symbols written 'h_0^\sigma', 'h_1^\sigma' in the transcription are l_0^\gamma, l_1^\gamma (generators to the power \gamma). The parametrization h_0 = g_0^{-1}\sigma_\infty(g_0)^{...} is not fully clear: the exponent is illegible. For a plain Z/2 coboundary it should simply be g_0^{-1}\sigma_\infty(g_0), possibly twisted by a power of l_0.

Surjectivity of the parametrizations (every 3-cocycle is one of the two given forms; every 2-cocycle is a coboundary) is asserted, not proved, on this page. It relies on the computation of H^1 of a finite cyclic group acting on a free profinite group, which needs justification (e.g. a profinite Kurosh-type argument for the semidirect product).

ideas.what: Parametrization of the automorphism group of the genus-0 Teichmueller tower by pairs (\xi, \gamma) with 2\gamma+1 a unit, a 3-cycle and a 2-cycle relation, plus (0,4) conditions.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990; Ihara; announced as a programme by Grothendieck in the Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme describes the idea qualitatively; explicit equations not published by him

ideas.what: Solving the 3-cycle relation as a (twisted) Z/3-coboundary \xi = \lambda\rho(\lambda)^{-1} or \lambda l_0^{-1}\rho(\lambda)^{-1}, with the case determined by p mod 3, and rewriting the 2-cycle relation as an equation in \lambda.
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1(Z/3, \hat F_2) and H^1(Z/2, \hat F_2) description of GT components; torsion/elliptic-point classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Partially in Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Ihara-school treatments of the 2- and 3-cycle relations (2-cycle as coboundary is standard)

ideas.what: Identification of the residual ambiguity (\lambda -> l_0^{-\alpha}\lambda), i.e. dependence on the tangential base point / inertia conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Conjugation by inertia, outer vs actual automorphisms, tangential base points

missed.claim: An explicit pre-Drinfeld cohomological reformulation of the GT-defining equations. The 3-cycle component is a Z/3-cocycle whose class (trivial vs the torsion-twisted class) is governed by the cyclotomic unit p = 2\gamma+1 mod 3. The 2-cycle component is a Z/2-coboundary. The full equation is then rewritten as a single 'equation in \lambda'.
missed.quote: on peut dire que les données des u ... équivalent à celles des solutions simultanées des deux équations de cocycles ... (suivant que \gamma≡0 (3) ou \gamma≡1 (3) i.e. p≡1 (3) ou p≡-1 (3))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The mod-3 dichotomy linking the cyclotomic character to the H^1(Z/3)-class of f is a neat structural statement about \widehat{GT}. It is not commonly stated in GT literature, which usually works with f modulo the 2-cycle as f = g^{-1}\sigma(g). It could give an alternative coordinate (\lambda) on \widehat{GT} and its Galois image.

missed.claim: Grothendieck wants to relate the g_0 in the Z/2-parametrization to other parameters (the note 'on pourrait mettre en rapport ce g_0 ...') and to view \lambda, g_0, h_0 as universal functions on the group (continued next page). This is not carried out here.
missed.quote: NB on pourrait mettre en rapport ce g_0 par g_0^{-1}...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are analogous to the 'universal functions' in Ihara's power-series/Galois-cocycle work. An explicit link between the Z/2 and Z/3 coboundary parameters remains a natural question.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a pre-Drinfeld, explicit form of the \widehat{GT} equations (with \gamma = m, p = \lambda), historically notable but consistent with what is known of Grothendieck's Longue Marche programme. The non-abelian H^1 reading with the p mod 3 case split is a modest unpublished detail. The mathematics is otherwise close to standard GT theory.
transcription_corrections: In (71), the factors 'h_1^\sigma ... h_0^\sigma' should read l_1^\gamma ... l_0^\gamma (powers of the generators by \gamma). In (72), read \lambda' = l_0^{-\alpha}\lambda, \gamma = \gamma'.
'De plus que (\lambda,\sigma) et (\lambda',\sigma') définissent' should read 'Pour que (\lambda,\gamma) et (\lambda',\gamma') définissent le même u, il faut et il suffit...'
'Au facteur cyclotomique h_0^\sigma près, que différencie h_0 et \xi_\sigma (65)' should read approximately 'Au facteur "cyclotomique" l_0^\gamma près, qui différencie h_0 et \xi (65)'.
'les ordonnées des u' should be 'les données des u'.
In (74), the case condition is on \gamma (\gamma≡0 (3) or \gamma≡1 (3), the latter apparently overwritten), not on \sigma. The variable is \xi, not \zeta.
